newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle Eaux to dominate Havas board - source.
newsitem.headline: Gle Eaux to dominate Havas board - source.

text.p: Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) will take control of the board of Havas at a March 28 Havas shareholders' meeting to approve its accord with CGE, a source close to the companies said.

The meeting is also due to approve the appointment of four CGE representatives to the Havas board, Havas and CGE spokesmen said. They will join Guy Dejouany, former CGE chairman and now its honorary chairman, who is already on the Havas board.
This will give CGE a third of the 15 board seats, but it can also count on support from other Havas board members, a source close to the companies said on Thursday.
Pierre Lescure, chairman of Canal Plus, which is involved in the reshuffle of assets and shareholdings contained in the CGE/Havas accord, is squarely in the CGE camp.

Other notable CGE allies are Marc Vienot, chairman of Societe Generale, Serge Tchuruk and Jean-Pierre Halbron, Alcatel Alsthom chairman and finance director respectively, and Belgian financier Albert Frere, boss of Audiofina, the source said.
Henri Lachmann, chairman of Strafor Facom, is nominated to replace Michel Francois-Poncet, chairman of Paribas's supervisory board who resigned from the Havas board recently.
Lachmann is close to Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier, as is CGE chairman Jean-Marie Messier, who is to be nominated to the Havas board along with three of his lieutenants on March 28.

The three are Guillaume Hannezo, CGE finance director, Eric Licoys, Messier's adviser, and Jean-Pascal Tranie, managing director of Compagnie Generale de Videocommunication (CGV), CGE's cable TV unit.
The Havas board has been marked by a number of defections of late. The most recent was Jerome Monod, chairman of Lyonnaise des Eaux, who resigned this week.
A CGE spokesman said three commissioners had been nominated by the chairman of the Paris industrial court to undertake the due diligence for the deal independently.
Philippe Lagayette, managing director of the Caisse des Depots et Consignations, and Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani, chairman of AGF, have also quit the Havas board.
If all the departures are replaced, the Havas board would again have 18 members, the number shown in its most recent annual report.
If all newcomers are approved at the March 28 meeting, CGE plus allies will represent some 50 percent of Havas capital and over half the seats on its board, the sources said.
Communication industry specialists say CGE's arrival in force on the board of Havas brings a welcome clarification of interests.
"It is clear that Generale des Eaux wants to wield power," a source close to the reshuffle said.

"Up to now Havas shareholders had contradictory interests which they put before the group's interests. Generale des Eaux will be able to set a strategy at Havas," said a sector analyst at a foreign bank.

Canal Plus's Lescure last October called for a simplification of Havas's shareholding base. "Such a collection of divergent interests among Havas's shareholders does not help it," Lescure said at the time.

Lyonnaise des Eaux, which still owns under one percent of Havas, has a stake in the TPS Digital satellite television group which rivals Canal Plus's Canalsatelite, operates thematic channel Paris Premiere and is a major shareholder in terrestrial channel M6, competitors on some fronts to Canal Plus.

This week France Telecom and Havas agreed to grant each other call and put options on Oda, a Havas unit which sells advertising space in France Telecom's telephone directories, which was another example of the tensions pervading Havas.

France Telecom does not want CGE, which has a declared aim of competing head-on with France Telecom after European telecommunications liberalisation next January, to have access to Oda. France Telecom had founded Oda as a 50-50 venture with Havas, but it had exchanged its Oda stake for a 4.4 percent stake in Havas.
